title: SDG Challenge: DSV Electric Fleet Charging
cardSummary: Led a student team on a sustainability and operations challenge for DSV's electric truck fleet. The wave-based charging workflow we proposed was implemented by DSV, reducing estimated operational costs by approximately 80%.

hero.description: A real-world sustainability and operations challenge for DSV, one of the world's largest logistics companies. Our team designed and proposed a wave-based charging workflow for their electric truck fleet, a solution DSV went on to implement, with initial estimates showing approximately 80% reduction in previously calculated operational costs.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body:
DSV operates a growing fleet of electric trucks and faced a set of interrelated operational problems stemming from inefficient charging practices:

- **Driver waiting time:** drivers were idling while vehicles charged, creating unnecessary cost and reducing effective working hours.
- **Unnecessary energy use:** charging was not aligned with operational schedules, leading to energy waste and off-peak inefficiencies.
- **Battery degradation:** uncoordinated charging patterns accelerated battery wear, increasing long-term maintenance and replacement costs.

The challenge was framed around sustainability and operational efficiency: find a solution that reduces cost, extends battery life, and fits within DSV's existing operational structure without requiring large infrastructure investment.

sections.heading: The proposed solution
sections.body:
Our team developed a **wave-based transportation and charging workflow** that decouples driver working time from vehicle charging time: the core insight being that a truck does not need a driver present while it charges.

- **Wave-based scheduling:** trucks are organized into departure and return waves, creating predictable windows when vehicles are available for charging without driver downtime.
- **Next-day operational charging:** charging is scheduled according to the next day's route requirements, ensuring trucks carry exactly the charge they need, avoiding both overcharging and undercharging.
- **Driver-vehicle decoupling:** drivers hand off vehicles at the depot rather than waiting on-site, freeing working hours and reducing operational overhead.

The solution was designed to integrate with DSV's existing fleet management workflows, minimizing change management friction while delivering measurable efficiency gains.

sections.heading: Results and impact
sections.body:
DSV evaluated the proposed workflow and moved to implement it on their electric fleet. Based on initial estimates at the time of implementation:

- **~80% reduction** in previously calculated operational costs associated with the charging process.
- Reduced driver waiting time tied to vehicle charging.
- More controlled charging cycles, reducing battery degradation risk over time.
- Energy use aligned with actual operational demand rather than ad-hoc availability.

This is the only project in Alejandro's portfolio where an external organization reviewed the work and committed to implementing it, making it the clearest evidence of real-world analytical and business impact.

Note: this is the DSV Electric Fleet Charging project, unrelated to RouteGuesser, which is a separate city-routing web game with no connection to DSV or logistics adoption.

sections.heading: Role as Team Captain
sections.body:
- **Problem framing:** structured the challenge into tractable sub-problems and kept the team focused on DSV's core operational constraints.
- **Analysis coordination:** directed the business analytics work, ensuring conclusions were grounded in data and operational reality.
- **Solution design:** led the development of the wave-based workflow concept and validated it against DSV's scheduling requirements.
- **Stakeholder communication:** presented the solution to DSV stakeholders, translating technical and operational logic into clear business language.
- **Change management:** addressed adoption barriers by designing a workflow that minimized disruption to existing processes.

sections.heading: What this project shows
sections.body:
- Applied analytical thinking on a real, ambiguous operations problem, not a pre-cleaned dataset or a defined task.
- Business case construction: identifying root causes, quantifying impact, and designing a feasible solution under real constraints.
- End-to-end ownership: from problem framing and analysis to stakeholder presentation and change management planning.
- Sustainability and operations domain knowledge: fleet electrification, charging logistics, and energy efficiency trade-offs.
- Leadership under pressure: managing team direction, priorities, and output quality in a time-constrained format.
